paragraphs: The 82-0 Basketball Builder is an independent roster-building game about one impossible basketball question: could your five-player lineup finish a full season undefeated?

Pick a playstyle, draft one player at a time from different teams and eras, then run the season simulation. Basketball fans love debating whether any roster could survive a full season without a loss — some lineups chase 82W–0L, while others fall short on defense, size, playmaking, or balance. The fun is seeing how your five performs once the full season is projected.

Each round gives you a random team and era. Choose one player from the available pool and place him into an open position on your lineup. Your playstyle controls the shape of the roster: balanced, small ball, twin towers, or run and gun.

You can draft with full stat lines visible, or turn stats off and rely on memory and instinct. After five picks, the simulator projects your roster across an 82-game season and gives you a final record, grade, strengths, and weaknesses.

The simulation engine aggregates your lineup's five statistical categories — scoring, rebounding, playmaking, steals, and blocks — and runs the total through a non-linear win curve. The relationship between stats and wins is not linear: as your team gets stronger, each additional win becomes significantly harder to earn. Going from 70 to 75 wins takes far more roster strength than going from 55 to 60.

On top of the curve, every category is gated. A deficiency in even one area — no rim protection, no playmaking — caps your ceiling and kills the perfect season, no matter how high your scoring total is. And different decades have different statistical environments: 30 points per game in the fast-paced 1960s is not worth the same as 30 in the 2020s, and the engine era-adjusts every stat line accordingly.

The 82-0 challenge rules are simple. One: each round, the slot machine assigns a random team and decade. Two: pick exactly one player from that roster. Three: place him at an open court position he actually played — PG, SG, SF, PF, or C. Four: you have one team skip and one era skip for the whole game. Five: after five picks, the engine simulates your season and projects a final record between 0-82 and 82-0, with a letter grade, your best pick, and your roster's biggest weakness. Share it and challenge your friends to beat it.

sections.h2: Tips to Build a Better Team
paragraphs: Maximize totals across all five categories. The engine has no synergy penalties — it rewards raw, era-adjusted production. But remember the gates: a lineup with zero blocks or zero playmaking caps your ceiling no matter how much it scores.

Mind your positions. Every pick must fit an open court slot the player actually played. Drafting a wing early at small forward can lock you out of a better wing later — keep your remaining slots in mind before you commit.
Know your eras. A 25-point scorer from the 2000s often beats a 30-point scorer from the 1960s after era adjustment. Pace-inflated numbers from older decades are quietly deflated by the engine.
Spend skips early, not late. If round one hands you a thin roster, skip immediately. Saving both skips for round five usually means wasting them.
Want a real test? Play Blind Draft mode — stats are hidden and you draft entirely from memory. It is the fastest way to find out who actually knows basketball history.

If you enjoy this game, you'll probably like other draft-style sports games — lineup builders, era debates, GOAT brackets, and fantasy drafts all scratch the same itch. The format runs for other sports too: 20-0 for the NFL, 38-0 for Premier League soccer, and 7-0 for the World Cup. What sets this one apart is that it gives every roster a clear, simulated result instead of an endless argument — your team either goes undefeated or it doesn't, and there's always another run.

whatIs.title: What Is 82-0? — Meaning & Basketball Roster Builder
whatIs.description: What does 82-0 mean in basketball? It is a perfect 82-game season — 82 wins, zero losses. Learn the idea, then build a roster and simulate your own season.
whatIs.intro: 82-0 means a perfect 82-game basketball season: 82 wins, zero losses. Learn the idea, then build a roster and see how close your team gets.

paragraphs: A professional basketball regular season is 82 games long. Going 82-0 means winning every single one of them — a perfect season. No team in league history has ever done it. The closest anyone has come is 73 wins, which means even the greatest team ever still lost nine times. That gap between 'greatest ever' and 'perfect' is what the number 82-0 represents, and it is why the phrase carries so much weight in basketball debates.

Because a perfect season has never happened, 82-0 became shorthand for an impossible standard. When fans say a lineup would 'go 82-0', they mean it is so stacked that it transcends normal competition.

The 82-0 challenge is a team building game born from that debate. The premise: you draft a five-player lineup of real basketball legends, but you don't get free choice — every pick comes from a randomly drawn team and decade. Chicago in the 1990s. Boston in the 1960s. Denver in the 2020s. From each draw you pick one player, place him at a court position he actually played, and after five picks your roster faces the question: would this team go 82-0?

The format rewards equal parts strategy and luck. Sometimes the slot machine hands you a dynasty; sometimes you are choosing between role players in round five with no skips left, and your perfect season dies on the spot. Every run is a new argument.

sections.h2: How Does the 82-0 Game Work Here?
paragraphs: Our version of the 82-0 challenge game runs entirely in your browser. Five rounds, one pick per round, one team skip and one era skip. Every player carries his real historical stat line — points, rebounds, assists, steals, and blocks per game — era-adjusted by the simulation engine, because 30 points in the 1960s is not 30 points in the 2020s. When your lineup is complete, the engine runs your aggregate totals through a non-linear win curve and projects a final record between 0-82 and 82-0. No download, no sign-up — and if you want a real test, Blind Draft mode hides the stats and makes you draft from memory.

Basketball arguments used to end in 'agree to disagree'. The 82-0 format gives them a scoreboard. Players share their projected records — 78-4, 80-2, the rare perfect 82-0 — and friends immediately try to beat them. It is a two-minute game with infinite replayability, built on top of a debate fans have been having for decades: which five players, across all of history, make the unbeatable team?

howItsCalculated.title: How Is 82-0 Calculated? The Scoring Engine Explained
howItsCalculated.description: How does the 82-0 challenge calculate your record? A plain-English breakdown of the five stat categories, the non-linear win curve, era adjustment, and why one weakness tanks a perfect season.
howItsCalculated.intro: Wondering how the 82-0 challenge turns five players into a win-loss record? Here is exactly what the simulation engine does, in plain English.

paragraphs: After you draft five players, the engine adds up their per-game stats across five categories — points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks — adjusts every line for the era it came from, then runs the total through a non-linear win curve to project a record between 0-82 and 82-0. A single weak category caps your ceiling no matter how strong the rest of the roster is.

Every player carries a real historical stat line: points (PPG), rebounds (RPG), assists (APG), steals (SPG) and blocks (BPG) per game. The engine sums each category across your starting five, so a lineup's scoring total is the sum of five scorers, its rebounding total the sum of five rebounders, and so on. Balance across all five matters more than a huge number in any one.
This is why a five-scorer lineup underperforms: it piles up points but posts near-zero blocks and playmaking, and the engine punishes that imbalance.

Total stat output does not translate to wins in a straight line. The engine runs your aggregate through a curve where each additional win costs progressively more roster strength. Going from 55 to 60 projected wins is cheap; going from 75 to 80 is brutally expensive. That curve is why 82-0 is so rare even with an elite lineup — the last few wins demand a near-perfect roster.

sections.h2: Category thresholds: why one hole sinks you
paragraphs: On top of the curve, every category has a minimum threshold. If your lineup has essentially no rim protection or no playmaking, the engine caps your projected record regardless of how high your scoring total climbs. A balanced 78-4 roster beats a lopsided 90-points-but-zero-blocks roster every time. This models real basketball: a team that cannot defend the rim or run an offense loses games no matter how much it scores.

30 points per game in the fast-paced, high-scoring 1960s is not the same as 30 points in the 2020s. The engine deflates pace-inflated numbers from older decades and normalizes every stat line to a common baseline before summing, so a player is not rewarded just for playing in a high-tempo era. This keeps cross-decade lineups fair.
The fastest way to understand the scoring is to play. Spin a lineup, read the projected record and the 'biggest weakness' callout, then tweak your next run to plug that hole.

Every category has a floor. A starting five with zero rim protection or zero playmaking limits your ceiling no matter how much it scores. Before you lock a pick, ask which category your roster is thinnest in and whether this player helps it.

A 25-point scorer from the 2000s often beats a 30-point scorer from the 1960s after era adjustment, because the engine deflates pace-inflated older numbers. When two picks look close, the more recent, more efficient era usually wins.

sections.h2: Can soccer or football actually go 82-0?
paragraphs: Not as a scoreline — goals are too hard to come by. The most lopsided official pro result ever was a freak 149-0 (a 2002 Madagascar protest match); a normal blowout rarely reaches double digits, and the Premier League's biggest margin is 9-0. But 82-0 was never really a scoreline. It is a perfect season: 82 games, 82 wins, zero losses — a basketball number, because an NBA regular season is 82 games long. Other sports have shorter seasons, so their 'perfect season' has a different number.

A Premier League season is 38 games, so soccer's version of the perfect undefeated season is 38-0. It is arguably harder than 82-0, because soccer draws so easily: Arsenal's legendary 2003-04 Invincibles went the whole season unbeaten and still only managed 26-12-0 — twelve draws short of a perfect 38-0. The 38-0 Challenge is the soccer edition of this exact game: spin Premier League clubs and eras, draft an XI of real legends, and chase the perfect season.

Want the international version? A World Cup run from the group stage to the final is seven matches, so a flawless tournament is 7-0. The 7-0 Challenge lets you build the greatest World Cup XI ever — mix legends from 1970 to 2026, link countrymen for chemistry, and chase a perfect 7-0 or survive a knockout gauntlet to lift the trophy.

If you searched 'football 82-0' meaning the NFL, the answer is 20-0. A modern Super Bowl run is 17 regular-season games plus three playoff rounds — win them all and you finish 20-0, something no team has done in the modern format (the 1972 Dolphins went 17-0 under the old schedule). The 20-0 Challenge drafts an NFL roster and simulates the whole run.

All four challenges share one idea: random team rolls, a draft built on real players, and a season simulation that decides whether your lineup survives undefeated. Pick your sport and chase the number — 82-0, 38-0, 20-0 or 7-0.

teamBuilder.title: 82-0 Team Builder
teamBuilder.description: Build your all-time basketball lineup with the 82-0 team builder. Slot machine draws, real legends from seven decades, simulated season record. Can you go undefeated?
teamBuilder.intro: Draft your five. Chase the perfect season. The team builder is right below — good luck.

paragraphs: This team builder is the heart of the 82-0 challenge. Every run spins up five random franchise-and-decade combinations spanning seven decades of basketball history — from the 1960s Celtics dynasty to the 2020s champions. Each draw offers the real players from that team and era, carrying their historical per-game stats across five categories, and the lineup you draft is simulated through a full 82-game season.

Because the draws are random, no two runs are alike. One game you are choosing between legends; the next you are squeezing wins out of role players with no skips left. The team builder rewards smart drafting: era awareness, category balance, position management, and knowing exactly when to burn a skip. Build, simulate, share, repeat — and see how close you can get to the impossible 82-0.

The engine aggregates five categories — points, rebounds, assists, steals, and blocks — after adjusting every stat line for its era's pace and scoring environment. The win curve is non-linear, so each additional win costs more roster strength than the last, and every category is gated: one glaring hole caps your projected record no matter how strong the rest of the roster is. Draft like a general manager, not a fan.

sevenZero.title: 7-0 Game: World Cup All-Time Dream Team Builder
sevenZero.description: Build the greatest World Cup XI ever. Mix legends from 1970 to 2026, stack countrymen for chemistry, run the knockout gauntlet, and chase a perfect 7–0. Free, no sign-up.
sevenZero.h1: 7-0 Game — All-Time World Cup Dream Team
sevenZero.intro: This is the deepest 7-0 builder we make: pull a single nation or an open World All-Stars pool, drop real players from eight decades into your formation, link countrymen for chemistry, then either chase a single flawless 7–0 or survive a four-round knockout gauntlet to lift the trophy.

sections.h2: World All-Stars: the cross-nation dream team
paragraphs: Most 7-0 games lock you to one country. This one adds a World All-Stars mode that throws open the doors: a single pool can hand you Pelé, Maradona, Cruyff and Zidane to line up in the same eleven. You are no longer building Brazil's best or France's best — you are building football's best, full stop.

But raw ratings are not enough. Chemistry rewards placing countrymen next to each other on the pitch, so the perfect All-Stars side is a balancing act between star power and national links. A team of eleven loners from eleven nations will look terrifying on paper and misfire on grass.

Single-match mode is the classic chase for one perfect 7–0. The gauntlet is the long road: your dream team must win four straight knockout rounds — group, round of 16, semi-final and final — against opponents that get stronger every step. Lose once and you are out; win all four and you are champions.

Because you keep the same squad through the bracket, the gauntlet rewards a deep, well-built eleven over a flat-track bully. You can tweak your line-up between rounds, so reading the next opponent and shifting your tactical style becomes part of the game.

Alongside the modern 2018, 2022 and 2026 squads, we added hand-picked legendary editions: Brazil 1970 and 2002, Argentina 1986, the Netherlands of 1974, West Germany 1990, France 1998, Italy 1982, England 1966, Spain 2010 and Uruguay 1950. Draw one of these and you are building with the players who actually defined the World Cup.
It means a single roll can send you eight decades back or drop you into a projected 2026 side — and in All-Stars mode, all of those eras share one player pool.

faqs.q: How is this different from the standalone 7-0 Game?
faqs.a: This in-site edition adds four things the standalone does not have: a cross-nation World All-Stars mode, a four-round knockout gauntlet, a chemistry system that rewards linking countrymen, and hand-built legendary squads from 1950 to 2010.
7–0 is the flawless scoreline. To earn it you need a high-rated eleven, every player in a position they truly fit, strong chemistry in All-Stars mode, and a tactical style that suits your squad.

In World All-Stars mode, each player links with their on-pitch neighbours. Neighbours from the same nation raise chemistry; isolated players lower it. Higher chemistry boosts your attack and defence, so clustering countrymen matters as much as raw ratings.

A knockout run of four rounds with rising difficulty. The same dream team must win all four — group, round of 16, semi-final and final — to be crowned champions. You can adjust your line-up between rounds.

faqs.q: Are the players and ratings real?
faqs.a: Player names are real, era-appropriate footballers and ratings are believable approximations for entertainment. This is an independent fan project, not affiliated with FIFA, any federation or club.
Yes. It is completely free, needs no account, runs in your browser, and is available in English, 中文, 日本語, 한국어, Español, Français and Deutsch. Your stats are saved locally on your device.

capMode.title: 82-0 Salary Cap Mode — The Strategic NBA Draft Game
capMode.description: A more strategic 82-0: build an NBA starting five under a fixed salary cap and chase an undefeated 82-game season without an unlimited superteam.
capMode.intro: A more strategic 82-0 NBA draft turned gauntlet. Every player has a price; you start with a loose budget and roll-and-pick your five. Go 82-0 and the budget tightens for the next level — how deep can you climb before a perfect season is unaffordable?

paragraphs: Cap Mode is the strategic twist on 82-0. Instead of an unlimited all-time superteam, every player carries a price and you build your starting five under a fixed salary cap. Spend it all on three megastars and you will have nothing left for the other two slots; spread it too thin and your team rating sags. The fun is in the trade-off.

Every player is priced from the same production score the engine uses to rate your team — points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks, adjusted for era. Prices run from about 5 for role players up to the low-30s for the all-time greats. You roll for teams and eras like classic 82-0, but only players you can still afford appear — and the game always reserves enough for your remaining spots, so you can't spend yourself into a dead end.

It plays as a gauntlet: you start with a generous budget and, every time you go 82-0, the budget tightens for the next level. A season that falls short of 82-0 ends the run, and how deep you climbed is your score. Any budget left unspent becomes a small efficiency bonus to your team rating.

A common winning shape is two or three priced-up stars plus cheap, efficient role players who fill the gaps. Because the engine punishes any single weak category, do not ignore defense — steals and blocks are baked into both the price and the win curve, so a cheap rim protector can be better value than another scorer.
Watch your positions too: a versatile guard or forward who fits multiple slots gives you more freedom to spend where it matters.

Cap Mode seasons are tagged on the global leaderboard so cap builders stand apart from classic runs. Climb the board by maximizing your team rating under budget — and if you go 82-0, the cap you left on the table is your edge over everyone else who did the same.

filter.title: 82-0 Challenge Filters — Cap, No MVPs, One Franchise & More
filter.description: Customize your 82-0 NBA challenge with draft filters: salary cap, no MVPs, one franchise, one decade, random era and hard mode.
filter.intro: Tired of the same random draft? Reshape your 82-0 NBA challenge with team-building filters — cap your budget, ban the MVPs, lock to one franchise or decade, or crank up Hard Mode.

paragraphs: The classic 82-0 challenge hands you random teams and eras to draft from. Challenge Filters give you control instead — reshape the draftable pool and the difficulty to make a harder, more deliberate run at the perfect season. Each filter also tags your leaderboard entry, so a No MVPs 82-0 reads very differently from an everyone-allowed one.

Salary Cap: a gauntlet where you roll your five under a budget that tightens every time you go 82-0 — the most strategic mode. No MVPs: the priciest all-time greats are banned, so you win without the icons. One Franchise: draft only from a single team's all-time roster. One Decade: lock the whole draft to one era of NBA history. Random Era: the game picks your decade for you. Hard Mode: a steeper win curve where even stacked rosters drop a few more games.

Hard Mode and Salary Cap are the toughest tests of a true 82-0. One Franchise and One Decade are medium — your ceiling depends on the team or era you pick. If you are new, start with Classic, then add filters one at a time as you learn which rosters actually survive 82 games.

noMvps.title: 82-0 No MVPs Challenge — Win Without the All-Time Greats
noMvps.description: Take the 82-0 NBA challenge with the priciest all-time greats banned. Build an undefeated starting five from role players and underrated stars.
noMvps.intro: The hardest bragging rights in basketball: go 82-0 without a single MVP-tier superstar. The ~35 priciest all-time greats are off the board — win with role players, glue guys and underrated stars instead.

sections.h2: What counts as an MVP here?
paragraphs: No MVPs mode bans the roughly 35 most valuable players in the pool — the all-time scoring and rebounding giants the engine prices highest. Everyone else is fair game, which means you are building from very good players rather than legends. It is the same roll-and-draft 82-0, just without the easy buttons.

Balance wins it. The engine punishes any single weak category, so spread your production across scoring, rebounding, assists, steals and blocks. Cheap rim protectors and high-assist guards carry more weight than another mid-volume scorer, and a versatile forward who covers two positions buys you flexibility. Hit every category and even a star-less five can chase a perfect season.

oneTeam.title: 82-0 One Franchise Challenge — One Team, Every Era
oneTeam.description: Build an undefeated 82-0 NBA starting five using only one franchise's all-time roster — Lakers, Celtics, Bulls, Spurs and more.
oneTeam.intro: Loyalty mode. Draft your entire 82-0 starting five from a single franchise's all-time roster — every Laker, every Celtic, every Bull across the decades. Can your team go undefeated on its own?

paragraphs: Pick a franchise from the menu and every roll in the draft is locked to that team — but across all eras of its history, so a 60s legend can line up next to a modern star. Only franchises with enough all-time depth to fill a balanced five are offered, so the draft never dead-ends.

The storied, deep franchises — the Lakers, Celtics, Bulls, Spurs and Warriors — field the most complete all-time fives and give you the best shot at a perfect season. Picking a younger or thinner franchise is the real challenge: you may be strong in one or two categories but exposed elsewhere, and the win curve will find the hole.

oneDecade.title: 82-0 One Decade Challenge — One Era, One Perfect Season
oneDecade.description: Lock your 82-0 NBA draft to a single decade of basketball history — the 60s, 80s, 90s, 2000s and beyond — and chase an undefeated season.
oneDecade.intro: Pick an era and live in it. Your whole 82-0 starting five must come from one decade of NBA history — the gritty 90s, the pace-and-space 2010s, your call. Which decade had the firepower to go undefeated?

paragraphs: Choose a decade and every team you roll is from that era — you build a five frozen in one moment of NBA history. The engine still adjusts each player's raw stats for the era they played in, so a 60s scoring title is not worth the same as a 90s one; the decade you pick shapes both who is available and how their numbers translate.

Every decade has a path to 82-0, but they win differently. The 90s and 2000s are stacked with two-way wings and dominant centers; the 80s bring elite playmaking and scoring; the 2010s and 2020s lean on shooting and switchable defense. Part of the fun is finding which era's strengths line up with the categories the win curve rewards.

hardMode.title: 82-0 Hard Mode — The Toughest Perfect-Season Challenge
hardMode.description: 82-0 with a steeper win curve. Even a stacked all-time starting five drops a few more games — only the very best rosters survive undefeated.
hardMode.intro: For players who find the perfect season too easy. Hard Mode steepens the win curve and tightens the 82-0 luck gate, so even a stacked all-time five drops a few more games. Only the very best rosters survive.

paragraphs: Hard Mode keeps the same all-time player pool but bends the math against you: the non-linear win curve gets a steeper exponent, so the same roster wins fewer games, and the gate for a true 82-0 is tightened. A five that cruises to 80-2 in the standard game might land at 76-6 here.

There is no margin for a weak category. Maximize scoring, rebounding, assists, steals and blocks all at once — any single hole drags the curve down harder than in the standard game. Prioritize two-way players who pad the defensive stats, and use your team and era re-rolls to chase the exact pieces your five is missing.
